questions.stem: Why does New York State want to turn off Niagara Falls?
options: A) To satisfy the curiosity of tourists.
B) To replace two old stone bridges.
C) To enable tourists to visit Goat Island.
D) To improve utility services in the state.

explain.定位:
The New York State parks system wants to turn off the falls on the American side sometime
in the next two to three years to replace two 115-year-old stone bridges that allow pedestrians,
park vehicles and utilities access to Goat Island.
纽约州公园系统打算在未来两到三年内的某个时候关掉瀑布的美国一侧，以便更换两座有
115年历史的石桥——这两座桥供行人、园区车辆和各类公用设施通往山羊岛。
explain.信号:
want to加to do的目的结构。这句靠想做某事加 to 表目的的结构成为答案句：wants to
turn off the falls 说出要做的事，紧跟的 to replace two 115-year-old stone bridges 用
不定式说出做这件事的目的——to do 前面是行为、后面就是原因，这正是预读里要盯的目
的信号。
explain.替换:
to replace two 115-year-old stone bridges ↔ To replace two old stone bridges.
数字年龄概括成old
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
To satisfy the curiosity of tourists. 看着诱人，是因为录音后面确实念到 People are
curious by nature.——好奇这个词真的出现过。但它出现在第3段讲人们天生好奇、想看底
下有什么，是关瀑布之后游客的反应，不是纽约州关瀑布的目的。听到 curious 就选，正中
原词陷阱。
借用原文：People are curious by nature.
C) 原词陷阱
To enable tourists to visit Goat Island. 诱人是因为录音 access to Goat Island 真的念到
了 Goat Island。但原文是说那两座桥供行人、车辆和公用设施通往山羊岛，山羊岛是桥的
功能去向，不是关瀑布去换桥的目的；而且原文说的是 pedestrians（行人）通行，并非专
为 tourists 去游览。盗用地名 Goat Island 来误导。
借用原文：utilities access to Goat Island
D) 偷换概念
To improve utility services in the state. 诱人是因为原文 utilities access to Goat Island
出现了 utilities（公用设施）一词。但原文只说桥让公用设施通往山羊岛，根本没说要改善
（improve）全州的公用服务。把设施通行偷换成改善服务，是借原词 utilities 制造的概念
偷换。
借用原文：park vehicles and utilities access to Goat Island

questions.stem: What did people find when Niagara Falls was shut off in 1969?
options: C) Lots of wrecked boats and ships.
D) Millions of coins on the bottom.

explain.定位:
In fact, those who first came to have a look did see something. They found millions of coins
on the bottom.
事实上，最先来看的那些人确实看到了点东西。他们在（瀑布）底部发现了数百万枚硬币。
explain.信号:
found后跟答案物。这句靠发现动词成为答案句：They found millions of coins on the
bottom. 直接用 found 点出人们发现的东西，found 后面紧跟的数量加事物就是答案落点
——这正是预读里要专门盯的 found 或 saw 类动词。
explain.替换:
millions of coins on the bottom ↔ Millions of coins on the bottom.
近乎原句照搬
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
Countless tree limbs.（数不清的树枝）听上去像河底常见之物，但录音从头到尾只说发现
了硬币，根本没提树枝。这是凭河底应该有树枝的常识想象出来的，原文无依据。
B) 与原文相反
A few skeletons. 有两处不对：一是 skeletons（骸骨）原文没提；二是数量 a few（很
少）与原文 millions（数百万，极多）正好相反。预读时已把 a few 与 millions 标成对立
点，正是要在这里听准多与少，别选反。
C) 未提及
Lots of wrecked boats and ships.（大量沉船）最像对，因为水底沉船太符合一般人对河
床的想象，画面感也强。但录音只说发现了 millions of coins，从未提及任何船只，这是典
型的常识陷阱，靠想当然填空。
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 The Tunisian government said Monday that 45 people have been killed after gunmen attacked a town
near the border with Libya.
突尼斯政府周一表示,武装分子袭击了与利比亚接壤的一个城镇,造成45人死亡。
2 The Interior and Defense ministries said that the Tunisian government has closed its two border
crossings with Libya because of the attack.
内政部和国防部表示,由于这次袭击,突尼斯政府已关闭了与利比亚的两个边境口岸。
3 The Tunisian military has sent reinforcements and helicopters to the area, and authorities have been
hunting several attackers who were still at large.
突尼斯军方已向该地区派遣增援部队和直升机,当局一直在追捕几名仍在逃的袭击者。
4 The violence came amid increasing international concern about Islamic State extremists in Libya.
Officials of the Tunisian government are especially worried after dozens of tourists were killed in the
attacks in Tunisia last year.
这次暴力事件发生之际,国际社会对利比亚的伊斯兰国极端分子的关注日益增加。突尼斯政府官员尤其担
忧,因为去年突尼斯发生的袭击事件中有数十名游客丧生。
5 Defense Minister Farhat Horchani said last week that German and American security experts were
expected to come to help Tunisia devise a new electronic video supervision system on its border
with Libya.
国防部长Farhat Horchani上周表示,预计德国和美国安全专家将前来帮助突尼斯在其与利比亚的边境设计
一套新的电子视频监控系统。
6 Tunisia was targeted last year by three attacks that left 70 people dead and were claimed by
Islamic State.
突尼斯去年成为三次袭击的目标,造成70人死亡,伊斯兰国宣称对这些袭击负责。

questions.stem: What did the Tunisian government do after the gunmen's attack?
options: A) It suspended diplomatic relations with Libya.
B) It urged tourists to leave Tunisia immediately.
C) It shut down two border crossings with Libya.
D) It launched a fierce attack against Islamic State.

explain.定位:
The Interior and Defense ministries said that the Tunisian government has closed its two
border crossings with Libya because of the attack.
内政部和国防部表示，由于这起袭击，突尼斯政府已关闭了它与利比亚之间的两个边境
口岸。
explain.信号:
主语应答＋ because of the attack 因果信号。这句以题干要找的主语 the Tunisian
government 出现，且带因果短语 because of the attack，正对应题干 after the
gunmen's attack——「因袭击而做了某事」，这一因果挂钩就是答案句信号。
explain.替换:
has closed its two border crossings with Libya ↔ shut down two border crossings with Libya
closed＝shut down 的同义替换
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
suspended diplomatic relations with Libya 借了录音里反复出现的 with Libya 来制造熟
悉感，但录音只说关闭口岸，从未提「中断外交关系」。听到 Libya 就选 A 正是原词陷
阱。
借用原文：two border crossings with Libya
B) 张冠李戴
urged tourists to leave Tunisia immediately 利用了录音第4段出现的 tourists 一词，但
那里讲的是去年有游客遇袭，并非政府这次「劝游客离开」。盗 tourists 充数，属张冠李戴
式诱导。
借用原文：dozens of tourists were killed
D) 与原文相反
launched a fierce attack against Islamic State 借了录音多次出现的 Islamic State，但录
音说的是政府关口岸、派增援搜捕在逃者，是防御搜捕，从未说「主动对 IS 发起猛攻」。
把守势说成攻势，是与原文相反的诱导。
借用原文：hunting several attackers who were still at large

questions.stem: What were German and American security experts expected to do in Tunisia?
options: A) Advise Tunisian civilians on how to take safety precautions.
B) Track down the organization responsible for the terrorist attack.
C) Train qualified security personnel for the Tunisian government.
D) Devise a monitoring system on the Tunisian border with Libya.

explain.定位:
Defense Minister Farhat Horchani said last week that German and American security experts
were expected to come to help Tunisia devise a new electronic video supervision system on
its border with Libya.
国防部长法尔哈特·霍尔查尼上周表示，预计德国和美国的安保专家将前来帮助突尼斯设计一
套位于其与利比亚边境上的新型电子视频监控系统。
explain.信号:
题干主语原样出现＋expected to 引出任务。这句原样出现题干主语 German and
American security experts，并用 were expected to come to help...devise 直接引出他
们的任务，「expected to + 帮助做某事」就是答案句信号。
explain.替换:
devise a new electronic video supervision system ↔ Devise a monitoring system
supervision system＝monitoring system 概括替换
on its border with Libya ↔ on the Tunisian border with Libya
its 还原为 the Tunisian，指代明确化
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
Advise Tunisian civilians on how to take safety precautions 蹭了录音的安保／边境氛
围，但录音说专家是来「建监控系统」，没说去「给平民支招防范」。任务对象与内容都不
符，属未提及的杜撰。
B) 张冠李戴
Track down the organization responsible for the terrorist attack 借了录音里的袭击／
在逃者氛围，但「搜捕在逃者」是突尼斯军方做的（第3段），不是德美专家的任务。把军
方的事安到专家头上，是张冠李戴。
借用原文：authorities have been hunting several attackers
C) 原词陷阱
Train qualified security personnel for the Tunisian government 借了录音里 security
experts 的 security 一词制造熟悉感，但录音说专家是来 help...devise system，没说来
「培训安保人员」。听到 security 就选 C 正是原词陷阱。
借用原文：German and American security experts

questions.stem: What did the three university students invent?
options: C) A plant-powered mobile phone charger.
D) A device to help plants absorb sunlight.

explain.定位:
Three university students in Santiago, Chile, have developed a plant-powered device to
charge their mobile phones.
智利圣地亚哥的三名大学生研发出了一种由植物供电、用来给手机充电的装置。
explain.信号:
新闻首句点题即答案句。新闻短消息的第一句往往就是核心事实。本句 have developed a
plant-powered device to charge their mobile phones 一上来就交代了“发明了什么”，正
是问“发明是什么”的答案句——信号就是“新闻开篇首句直接报核心”。
explain.替换:
a plant-powered device to charge their mobile phones ↔ A plant-powered mobile phone charger
“给手机充电的装置”=“手机充电器”
explain.排除:
A) 偷换概念
An environment-friendly battery. 把发明说成“环保电池”。录音从头到尾说的是 charge
（充电）的 device，从未称其为 battery（电池）；充电器和电池是两种东西，属未提及的
张冠李戴。
B) 原词陷阱
An energy-saving mobile phone. 借了录音里反复出现的原词 mobile phones 来制造熟
悉感，但发明是“给手机充电的装置”，不是“一部省电手机”。听到 mobile phone 就想选，
正中原词陷阱。
借用原文：to charge their mobile phones
D) 与原文相反
A device to help plants absorb sunlight. 凑齐了 plant、sunlight 等话题词，却把方向反
了：发明是“收集植物产生的能量给手机充电”，不是“帮植物吸收阳光”。属与原文相反的方
向倒置。
借用原文：converting sunlight into energy

questions.stem: When did they get the idea for the invention?
options: A) While sitting in their school's courtyard.
B) While playing games on their phones.
C) While solving a mathematical problem.
D) While doing a chemical experiment.

explain.定位:
The three engineering students got the idea for the device while sitting in their
school's courtyard.
这三名工程系学生是在坐在学校的院子里时想到了这个装置的点子。
explain.信号:
while 引导时间状语即答案。本句的信号词是 while sitting in their school's courtyard 里
的 while——题目问 When，答案就锁在 while 引导的这个时间状语上：他们是“坐在学校
院子里时”产生灵感的。
explain.替换:
while sitting in their school's courtyard ↔ While sitting in their school's courtyard.
状语近乎原样照搬
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
While playing games on their phones. 借了录音反复出现的 mobile phones 原词，编出
“玩手机游戏时”的场合，但录音说的是坐在院子里，并无“玩游戏”。听到 phone 就选，正中
原词陷阱。
借用原文：mobile phones
C) 未提及
While solving a mathematical problem. 是凭“理工科学生 = 在解题”的常识脑补的场景，
录音从未提到解数学题，属未提及。
D) 未提及
While doing a chemical experiment. 最贴“搞发明”的直觉，但录音说的是 engineering
students（工程系）在 courtyard（院子）想到的，既没提化学、也没提做实验，属未提及
的诱惑项。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the invention?
options: A) It increases the applications of mobile phones.
B) It speeds up the process of photosynthesis.
C) It improves the reception of mobile phones.
D) It collects the energy released by plants.

explain.定位:
It captures the energy which plants produce during photosynthesis—a process of converting
sunlight into energy.
它捕获植物在光合作用过程中产生的能量——光合作用是把阳光转化为能量的过程。
explain.信号:
功能描述句直说原理。信号是录音对装置功能的直接陈述 It captures the energy which
plants produce（它捕获植物产生的能量）。问“关于发明说了什么”，就锁这种“It + 它干了
什么”的功能句。第 3 段 E-Kaia collects that energy 再次印证“收集能量”这一核心功能。
explain.替换:
It captures the energy which plants produce ↔ It collects the energy released by plants
captures=collects、produce↔released
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
It increases the applications of mobile phones. 借录音原词 mobile phones 编出“增加
手机应用”的功能，但录音只说它给手机充电、没说增加应用。原词在、功能假。
借用原文：to charge their mobile phones
B) 原词陷阱
It speeds up the process of photosynthesis. 借了录音原词 photosynthesis，但装置是
“利用/捕获”光合作用产生的能量，绝非“加快”光合作用。听到 photosynthesis 就选，正中
原词陷阱。
借用原文：the energy which plants produce during photosynthesis
C) 原词陷阱
It improves the reception of mobile phones. 又一次借 mobile phones 原词，编出“改
善手机信号”的功能，但 reception（信号接收）录音根本没提，装置只负责充电。
借用原文：to charge their mobile phones

questions.stem: What did the man do before the telephone conversation?
options: A) He visited the workshops in the Grimsby plant.
B) He called the woman and left her a message.
C) He used stand-ins as replacements on all lines.
D) He asked a technician to fix the broken production line.

explain.定位:
Hello, Jeff. It's Helen. I got your message on the answering machine.
你好，杰夫。我是海伦。我收到了你留在答录机上的留言。
explain.信号:
对方应答里反证了"留言"动作。答案信号是被叫方 Helen 一开口的回应 I got your
message on the answering machine\\——她"收到了留言"，反推出通话前男方做的事正
是"打电话留了言"。这种"由对方的话反证某人做过某事"是对话题常见的答案信号，不一定
由本人正面说出。
explain.替换:
I got your message on the answering machine ↔ He called the woman and left her a message.
"收到留言"反推为"打电话留言"
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
He visited the workshops in the Grimsby plant. 借用了录音里真出现的 the Grimsby
plant\\，让你一听到"格里姆斯比工厂"就想选它。但录音只说该厂的生产线出了故障，从没
说男方"参观了车间"——盗了地名却安了个没发生的动作。
借用原文：the Grimsby plant
C) 原词陷阱
He used stand-ins as replacements on all lines. 抓了录音热词 stand-ins\\（备用机），
但录音说的是 Can't you replace them with the stand-ins? 只是女方在"提议"用备用机，
男方还回答"不行"；而且备用机只在 Line 6 用着，绝非"用在所有线上"。盗了热词又把范围
夸大成 all lines。
借用原文：Can't you replace them with the stand-ins?
D) 张冠李戴
He asked a technician to fix the broken production line. 把录音后段提到的"修理"和"工
程师"凑成一个动作。但录音里 That's what the maintenance engineer says. 只是工程
师"估了修要一周"，男方并没有"叫技工去修线"这个通话前的动作——人物和动作被硬拼到
一起了。
借用原文：That's what the maintenance engineer says.

questions.stem: What does the man say about Line 3 in the Grimsby plant?
options: A) It is the most modern production line.
C) It has stopped working completely.
D) It is going to be upgraded soon.

explain.定位:
Well, it's the Grimsby plant again, I'm afraid. The robots on Line 3 have gone wrong. And the
line is at a standstill.
唉，恐怕又是格里姆斯比工厂的事。三号线上的机器人出故障了，整条线停摆了。
explain.信号:
故障+停摆的状态陈述。答案信号是男方对 Line 3 直接给出的状态描述：The robots on
Line 3 have gone wrong 加上 the line is at a standstill\\——"出故障"+"停摆"连在一
起，就是这道状态题的落点。听到对象词 Line 3 后紧跟的"坏了/停了"就该锁定。
explain.替换:
the line is at a standstill ↔ It has stopped working completely.
at a standstill=完全停了
The robots on Line 3 have gone wrong ↔ It has stopped working completely.
gone wrong 佐证"停止运转"
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
It is the most modern production line. 说 Line 3 是"最现代的生产线"，但录音从头到尾
只讲它坏了、停了，没有一句夸它先进。这是凭空添加的好评，与原文负面状态相反。
B) 原词陷阱
It assembles super-intelligent robots. 抓了全程热词 robots，让你听到 robots 就想选。
但录音里 The robots on Line 3 是说"线上的机器人坏了"，机器人是"在线上干活的设备"，
绝不是说这条线"组装机器人"——盗了热词却编了个生产内容。
借用原文：The robots on Line 3
D) 偷换概念
It is going to be upgraded soon. 把录音后面 About a week.\\（修理约需一周）的"修
复"偷换成"升级"。修坏了的线≠升级，而且时间指向的是"修复工期"，不是"即将升级"——
动作和指向都被改了。
借用原文：About a week.

questions.stem: What is the man's purpose in calling the woman?
options: B) To place an order for robots.
C) To request her to return at once.
D) To ask for Tom's phone number.

explain.定位:
Not yet, Helen. I thought I'd better get your OK first.
还没呢，海伦。我想我最好先得到你的同意。
explain.信号:
"I'd better…first"道出真实意图。答案信号是男方主动表态的句子 I thought I'd better
get your OK first\\——"我得先取得你的同意"，这是他打电话的真实诉求。目的题的落点
常是 I'd better… / I thought I'd… 这种"我打算/我最好"的意图句，听到就要抓。
explain.替换:
get your OK first ↔ To seek her permission.
get your OK=求许可
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
To place an order for robots. 借了热词 robots，但录音里机器人是"坏掉要修"的设备 The
robots on Line 3 have gone wrong\\，全程没人提"下订单买机器人"。盗了热词编了个不
存在的目的。
借用原文：The robots on Line 3 have gone wrong
C) 与原文相反
To request her to return at once. 说目的是"让她立刻回来"，但录音里男方反倒在结尾道
歉 Sorry to spoil your day off\\，是体谅她在休息、没打算叫她回来。方向正好相反。
借用原文：Sorry to spoil your day off
D) 原词陷阱
To ask for Tom's phone number. 借了录音真出现的人名 Tom，让你一听到 Tom 就上
钩。但 Get on the phone to Tom 是女方让男方"去给 Tom 打电话"，根本不是男方"向她
要 Tom 的号码"——盗了人名却安了个相反的动作。
借用原文：Get on the phone to Tom

questions.stem: Where is the woman at the time of the conversation?
options: B) She is having her day off.
C) She is on sick leave.
D) She is abroad on business.

explain.定位:
Sorry to spoil your day off.
抱歉打扰了你的休息日。

The Secret to Raising Smart Kids

A) I first began to investigate the basis of human motivation—and how people persevere after setbacks—as a psychology graduate student at Yale University in the 1960s. After such an experience an animal often remains passive even when it can effect change—a state they called learned helplessness.

B) People can learn to be helpless, too. Why do some students give up when they encounter difficulty, whereas others who are no more skilled continue to strive and learn? One answer, I soon discovered, lay in people's beliefs about why they had failed.

C) In particular, attributing poor performance to a lack of ability depresses motivation more than does the belief that lack of effort is to blame. When I told a group of school children who displayed helpless behavior that a lack of effort led to their mistakes in math, they learned to keep trying when the problems got tough. Another group of helpless children who were simply rewarded for their success on easier problems did not improve their ability to solve hard math problems. These experiments indicated that a focus on effort can help resolve helplessness and generate success.

D) Later, I developed a broader theory of what separates the two general classes of learners—helpless versus mastery-oriented. I realized these different types of students not only explain their failures differently, but they also hold different "theories" of intelligence. The helpless ones believe intelligence is a fixed characteristic: you have only a certain amount, and that's that. I call this a "fixed mind-set(思维模式)." Mistakes crack their self-confidence because they attribute errors to a lack of ability, which they feel powerless to change. They avoid challenges because challenges make mistakes more likely. The mastery-oriented children, on the other hand, think intelligence is not fixed and can be developed through education and hard work. Such children believe challenges are energizing rather than intimidating(令人生畏); they offer opportunities to learn. Students with such a growth mind-set were destined(注定) for greater academic success and were quite likely to outperform their counterparts.

E) We validated these expectations in a study in which two other psychologists and I monitored 373 students for two years during the transition to junior high school, when the work gets more difficult and the grading more strict, to determine how their mind-sets might affect their math grades. At the beginning of seventh grade, we assessed the students' mind-sets by asking them to agree or disagree with statements such as "Your intelligence is something very basic about you that you can't really change." We then assessed their beliefs about other aspects of learning and looked to see what happened to their grades.

They understood that even geniuses have to work hard. Confronted by a setback such as a disappointing test grade, students with a growth mind-set said they would study harder or try a different strategy. The students who held a fixed mind-set, however, were concerned about looking smart with less regard for learning. They had negative views of effort, believing that having to work hard was a sign of low ability. They thought that a person with talent or intelligence did not need to work hard to do well. Attributing a bad grade to their own lack of ability, those with a fixed mind-set said that they would study less in the future, try never to take that subject again and consider cheating on future tests.

As a result, their math grades overtook those of the other students by the end of the first semester—and the gap between the two groups continued to widen during the two years we followed them.

For instance, talking about mathematical geniuses who were more or less born that way puts students in a fixed mind-set, but descriptions of great mathematicians who fell in love with math and developed amazing skills produce a growth mind-set.

I designed an eight-session workshop for 91 students whose math grades were declining in their first year of junior high. Forty-eight of the students received instruction in study skills only, whereas the others attended a combination of study skills sessions and classes in which they learned about the growth mind-set and how to apply it to schoolwork. In the growth mind-set classes, students read and discussed an article entitled "You Can Grow Your Brain." They were taught that the brain is like a muscle that gets stronger with use and that learning prompts the brain to grow new connections. From such instruction, many students began to see themselves as agents of their own brain development. questions.stem: What did Adam Smith say about sugar, alcohol and tobacco?
options: A) They were profitable to manufacture.
B) They were in ever-increasing demand.
C) They were subject to taxation almost everywhere.
D) They were no longer considered necessities of life.
questions.passage:
"Sugar, alcohol and tobacco," economist Adam Smith once wrote, "are commodities which are nowhere necessaries of life, which have become objects of almost universal consumption, and which are, therefore, extremely popular subjects of taxation."

Two and a half centuries on, most countries impose some sort of tax on alcohol and tobacco. With surging obesity levels putting increasing strain on public health systems, governments around the world have begun to toy with the idea of taxing sugar as well.

Whether such taxes work is a matter of debate. A preliminary review of Mexico's taxation found a fall in purchases of taxed drinks as well as a rise in sales of untaxed and healthier drinks. By contrast, a Danish tax on foods high in fats was abandoned a year after its introduction, amid claims that consumers were avoiding it by crossing the border to Germany to satisfy their desire for cheaper, fattier fare.

The food industry has, in general, been firmly opposed to such direct government action. Nonetheless, the renewed focus on waistlines means that industry groups are under pressure to demonstrate their products are healthy as well as tasty.

Over the past three decades, the industry has made some efforts to improve the quality of its offerings. For example, some drink manufacturers have cut the amount of sugar in their beverages.

Many of the reductions over the past 30 years have been achieved either by reducing the amount of sugar, salt or fat in a product, or by finding an alternative ingredient. More recently, however, some companies have been investing money in a more ambitious undertaking: learning how to adjust the fundamental make-up of the food they sell. For example, having salt on the outside, but none on the inside, reduces the salt content without changing the taste.

While reformulating recipes(配方) is one way to improve public health, it should be part of a multi-sided approach. The key is to remember that there is not just one solution. To deal with obesity, a mixture of approaches—including reformulation, taxation and adjusting portion sizes—will be needed. There is no silver bullet.

Excessively skinny models have been a point of controversy for decades, and two researchers say a model's body mass should be a workplace health and safety issue. questions.stem: What are Record and Austin advocating in the Monday editorial?
options: A) A change in the public's view of female beauty.
B) Government legislation about models' weight.
C) Elimination of forced weight loss by models.

questions.passage:
You may have heard some of the fashion industry horror stories: models eating tissues or cotton balls to hold off hunger, and models collapsing from hunger-induced heart attacks just seconds after they step off the runway.

Excessively skinny models have been a point of controversy for decades, and two researchers say a model's body mass should be a workplace health and safety issue. In an editorial released Monday in the American Journal of Public Health, Katherine Record and Bryn Austin made their case for government regulation of the fashion industry.

The average international runway model has a body mass index (BMI) under 16—low enough to indicate starvation by the World Health Organization's standard. And Record and Austin are worried not just about the models themselves, but about the vast number of girls and women their images influence.

"Especially girls and teens," says Record. "Seventy percent of girls aged 10 to 18 report that they define perfect body image based on what they see in magazines." That's especially worrying, she says, given that anorexia(厌食症) results in more deaths than does any other mental illness, according to the National Institute of Mental Health.

It's commonly known that certain diseases are linked with occupations like lung disease in coal miners. Professional fashion models are particularly vulnerable to eating disorders resulting from occupational demands to maintain extreme thinness.

Record's suggestion is to prohibit agents from hiring models with a BMI below 18.

In April, France passed a law setting lower limits for a model's weight. Agents and fashion houses who hire models with a BMI under 18 could pay $82,000 in fines and spend up to 6 months in jail. Regulating the fashion industry in the United States won't be easy, Record says. But with the new rules in France, U.S. support could make a difference. "A designer can't survive without participating in Paris Fashion Week", she says, adding, "Our argument is that the same would be true of New York Fashion Week."

writing.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay. Suppose you have two options upon graduation: one is to work in a state-owned business and the other in a joint venture. You are to make a choice between the two. When it comes to choosing a career after graduation, I would rather work in a joint venture than in a state-
owned business. Though both offer decent prospects, I am firmly convinced that a joint venture suits me better.
The main reason is that a joint venture provides a more competitive environment, where personal ability, rather
than seniority, decides how far one can go. What attracts me most is the chance to work with foreign
colleagues, learn advanced management skills and improve my English in daily practice. Besides, such
companies usually offer higher salaries and reward hard work generously, which matters a lot to a fresh
graduate like me. A state-owned business, by contrast, tends to be stable but slow, where a young talent may
easily be buried by dull routine.
For these reasons, I will not hesitate to choose a joint venture, because it offers exactly the growth and
challenge that a young person truly needs.
